transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Eric Huang (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Larkfield HoS), Priya Menon (Platform Eng), Olivia Chen (IT Ops), Markus Vogel (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on SAML/SCIM-based provisioning and an RBAC/least-privilege model for Redwood integration. Discussed Okta as IdP, group->role mapping, audit log retention, KMS options for envelope encryption, and data residency constraints for EU workloads. Agreed on next steps: share security artifacts, exchange role mapping examples, schedule staging pilot.

Topics:
- SAML SSO flow (IdP initiated vs SP) and redirect URIs
- SCIM SCHEMA, attribute mapping and provisioning cadence
- RBAC role definitions, service accounts, and least-privilege principles
- Audit logging, retention, and log delivery (syslog/S3/Kafka)
- Encryption at rest: customer-managed KMS/HSM vs Redwood-managed keys
- Data residency and region pinning (EU production requirement)

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round — introduce yourselves?
[00:12] Jamal Ortiz: Hey, Jamal here, head of security at Larkfield. We manage the infra and compliance.
[00:18] Priya Menon: Priya, platform eng — I'll be the primary contact for integrations.
[00:23] Olivia Chen: Olivia, ops — will handle VPC/network and allowlists.
[00:28] Markus Vogel: Markus, compliance team — SOC 2 and internal audits.
[00:33] Maya Patel: Great. Eric, you wanna breathe through agenda?
[00:36] Eric Huang: Sure. We'll walk SSO (SAML) options, SCIM provisioning for users/groups, propose an RBAC matrix for least privilege, and then go over audit logs and KMS options. We'll leave 10–15 for Q/A.

[02:05] Eric Huang: To start SAML — Larkfield said you're on Okta, correct?
[02:12] Priya Menon: Correct, Okta org across the company. We also have a couple of service accounts in AD sync.
[02:18] Eric Huang: Cool. Redwood supports both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. For onboarding speed we usually do IdP-initiated first, because it avoids redirect configuration on multiple subdomains, but SP-initiated is recommended for tighter control and can be done for production.
[02:35] Jamal Ortiz: We prefer SP-initiated for auditability, but IdP-initiated would be fine for the pilot.
[02:42] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll set pilot as IdP-initiated then switch to SP in prod.

[05:10] Eric Huang: SCIM — we can consume groups and user attributes. Our recommended attributes are: userName, externalId, emails, displayName, and custom "redwood_roles" group mapping. We also support incremental syncs; default polling is every 5 minutes but can be tuned.
[05:28] Priya Menon: For us, group cadence is important — Okta creates groups per product team and per environment. Can Redwood map multiple groups to a single role?
[05:37] Eric Huang: Yes, one role in Redwood can be mapped to multiple Okta groups. Example: dev-team-a and dev-team-a-readmap can both map to the same Redwood "developer" role but with different privileges if you want. Slight caveat: SCIM group nesting isn't universally supported in all IdPs; Okta flattens groups in our experience.
[06:00] Oliveira Chen: (transcription: "Olivia") We have nested AD -> Okta sync, so please be aware some group names may carry AD domain prefixes.
[06:08] Eric Huang: Good flag. We can do a small normalization step on import. We'll want a sample CSV/export to validate mapping.

[09:20] Jamal Ortiz: On RBAC, our primary ask is least privilege. We want to ensure that devs can't escalate to billing or infra roles. What's Redwood's recommended role set?
[09:32] Maya Patel: We typically recommend a three-layer baseline: Admin (full), Developer (deploy/inspect but no billing), Viewer (read-only). Then create service roles for automated jobs and a dedicated "SRE" role with elevated metrics access.
[09:47] Eric Huang: I'll add nuance — we support attribute-based policies too, so you can restrict per-environment or per-namespace. Example: allow developer role to create model endpoints only in staging.
[10:05] Priya Menon: That attribute-based piece is useful. We need to carve access per-tenant for our customers. Can Redwood scope down to tenant IDs?
[10:12] Eric Huang: Yes, resource tags and tenancy scoping are supported. We'll show a role matrix sample.

[12:40] Markus Vogel: From a compliance view: audit logs need to be immutable and retained for at least 365 days, with export to our SIEM. Do you support pushing logs to our S3 bucket or to a syslog endpoint?
[12:55] Eric Huang: We currently support delivery to customer S3 (encrypted), syslog over TLS, and event streaming via Kafka connectors. Also have an internal retention policy for hosted accounts but for Dedicated/Private you can control retention.
[13:15] Jamal Ortiz: For this engagement we'll need logs to go to our EU S3 bucket and also push critical events to our Splunk instance.
[13:24] Eric Huang: Ok — Splunk forwarding via syslog/TCP TLS is feasible. We will need a TLS cert and endpoint details. For S3 delivery, we'll support SSE-KMS.

[16:00] Olivia Chen: About KMS — our security team prefers CMK in our AWS account, but we also evaluate HSMs for higher assurance. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[16:12] Eric Huang: Yes. For Private deployments or Dedicated we can integrate with customer-managed KMS; for hosted we also support envelope encryption with customer CMK via cross-account grants. For HSM, we have an HSM pass-through option for certain enterprise plans but that requires network connectivity and key ceremony planning.
[16:36] Jamal Ortiz: Network connectivity — we'll want to know what ports and egress are required. Olivia, please capture that for action item.

[18:50] Maya Patel: Quick question on PII/data residency — Larkfield requires EU residency for production models. Can we pin workloads to eu-west-1?
[19:01] Eric Huang: Yes. Redwood supports region pinning per model or per deployment. For hosted, you can request EU-only tenancy; for Dedicated/Private it's configurable. Keep in mind some public embeddings cache might have cross-region implications unless disabled. We'll show the setting to disable cross-region cache.

[22:30] Priya Menon: If we do SCIM provisioning, what's user lifecycle behaviour? Deprovision immediately, or soft-delete? We need it to lock access within 5 minutes of Okta deactivation.
[22:43] Eric Huang: SCIM deprovisioning is near real-time — within 1–5 minutes typically. We can do immediate disable and then a configurable retention for audit logs.
[23:10] Jamal Ortiz: Perfect. For our SOC 2 controls we need demonstrable revocation windows. Can you provide timelines in writing?
[23:19] Maya Patel: We'll include the SLA and expected sync windows in the security pack.

[27:00] Markus Vogel: On role elevation requests — do you support just-in-time approvals or time-bound grants?
[27:12] Eric Huang: We don't provide a built-in approval workflow yet, but we support time-bound API tokens and temporary role bindings that an orchestration layer (like your internal tool) can create. We can also integrate with external approval systems via webhooks.
[27:35] Priya Menon: Okay, we may want a time-bound devops_elevate role — 30 minute max. Is that possible?
[27:42] Eric Huang: Yes, short-lived bindings are supported; we'll document the API flow.

[31:20] Olivia Chen: Network questions: for a staging pilot, what are the allowlist IPs and do you support VPC peering?
[31:30] Eric Huang: For Dedicated/Private we support VPC peering and private endpoints. For hosted, we provide static egress IP ranges and can set up client TLS with mTLS optional. We'll send a network requirements doc.

[34:00] Jamal Ortiz: A couple of nitty-gritty items — LDAP/AD group name mangling, SCIM custom attributes, and the need to map our internal cost-center tags to Redwood tenant tags. Can that be ingested?
[34:18] Eric Huang: We support custom SCIM attribute mappings and tag propagation on resources. Cost-center tags can be passed as metadata on resource creation and used in billing export.

[37:50] Maya Patel: On the pilot scope — propose: 1) SCIM provisioning of a 30-user test group, 2) SAML IdP-initiated login testing, 3) basic RBAC matrix enforcement in staging, 4) audit log export to their EU S3. Should take about 1–2 sprints. Thoughts?
[38:05] Priya Menon: That aligns with our plan. We'll allocate 2 platform sprint days and a few security review hours.
[38:12] Jamal Ortiz: From compliance, we want to run an audit checklist after pilot.
[38:18] Markus Vogel: Also require a short runbook for incident response around leaked tokens.

[42:00] Eric Huang: Quick demo screen-share note — we'll send a recording of a quick demo of the RBAC mapping UI and the SCIM logs so you can review the webhook payloads.

[45:35] Priya Menon: One more question — team-service accounts for CI. How do we safely provision API keys?
[45:42] Eric Huang: Use short-lived API keys, tie them to service roles and rotate via your secrets manager. For CI we recommend instance role exchange via OIDC / token exchange rather than long-lived keys.
[46:05] Jamal Ortiz: Does Redwood log key creation and usage with user identity attached?
[46:12] Eric Huang: Yes, keystore events are recorded and included in audit stream.

[50:10] Markus Vogel: Any known compliance gaps we should be aware of?
[50:17] Maya Patel: For most customers the big items are: key custody model (customer vs Redwood), log retention config, and region pinning. If you require a dedicated HSM or an on-prem control plane we can propose Private. We'll include tradeoffs in the pack.

[54:00] Olivia Chen: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[54:03] Maya Patel: Recap — Redwood to share: SOC2 + ISO summary, SCIM schema example, network requirements, and RBAC sample matrix. Larkfield to share: Okta group export, sample users, and S3 plus Splunk endpoints. Schedule pilot for week of Aug 23. SE will run staging smoke tests by Aug 17.
[54:29] Priya Menon: Confirmed.
[54:31] Jamal Ortiz: Confirmed.

[56:00] Maya Patel: Anything else?
[56:04] Markus Vogel: One ask — can you include a timeline for compliance artifacts we can present to auditors?
[56:10] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll include a one-pager timeline and evidence locations.

[61:30] Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email and attach the security pack.
[61:38] Eric Huang: Thanks, everyone.
[61:42] Meeting ended.
